Rashi on Nazir 23a:10:1.hebrew: אבל אשה דהפר לה בעלה - דקאי גבה בהתירא, אימא לא תיבעי סליחה:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:10:1.english: However, a woman whose husband nullified [her vow] - Since with respect to her it stands permitted, say [that] she does not require forgiveness.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:11:1.hebrew: אבל בשתי חתיכות - אחת של חלב ואחת של שומן, כההיא דאיסי בן יהודה:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:11:1.english: However, in [the case of] two pieces - One of forbidden fat and one of [permitted] fat, like that [case] of Isi ben Yehuda:

Rashi on Nazir 23a:11:2.english: Where the prohibition is established - For at any rate, he knew that one of them was [forbidden] fat.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:11:3.english: I would say: Let atonement and forgiveness not suffice for him - For he is considered like an intentional [transgressor].

Rashi on Nazir 23a:11:4.hebrew: קמ"ל דלא שנא - ידע כולו, ולא שנא ידע מקצתו — מביא אשם תלוי ומתכפר לו:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:11:4.english: It teaches us that it is no different - [Whether] he knew [of the prohibition] entirely, or whether he knew [of it only] partially, he brings a suspensive guilt-offering and achieves atonement.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:12:1.hebrew: ואחד אכלו לשם אכילה גסה - או מחמת תאוה, שאכלו ברעבון:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:12:1.english: And one ate it for the sake of excessive eating - Or out of craving, in that he ate it ravenously.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:14:1.hebrew: מי דמי אנן אמרינן דבחד דרך - הולך אחד, ונכשל אחד:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:14:1.english: Is it comparable? We said that on one path - One walks, and one stumbles:

Rashi on Nazir 23a:14:2.hebrew: והכא שני דרכים - אשתו ואחותו, דלזה נזדמנה לו אשתו, ולזה אחותו:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:14:2.english: And here, [there are] two paths - [Namely,] his wife and his sister; for to this one, his wife presented herself, and to that one, his sister.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:15:1.english: This entire verse is stated with regard to sin - And therefore, you cannot judge him favorably.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:1:1.hebrew: ומתניתין דאמר הריני נזיר לגמרי ואת מאי - כלומר: ואת, מי הוית נזירה? והלכך, אי אמרה "אמן", דניחא לה בנזירות — הרי בעל יכול להפר, לפי שלא תלה נדרו בנדרה (ומתני' דקתני דיכול להפר את שלה, וברייתא קתני דשניהן יכול להפר):
Rashi on Nazir 23a:1:1.english: And the mishna [is referring to a case] where he said, "I am hereby a nazirite" completely, "and what [about] you?" - That is to say: And you, would you become a nazirite? And therefore, if she said "Amen," as she is pleased with naziriteship, behold, the husband can nullify [her vow], since he did not make his vow dependent upon her vow (and the mishna teaches that he can nullify hers, while the baraita teaches that he can nullify [the vows of] both of them).

Rashi on Nazir 23a:20:1.hebrew: אח נפשע זה לוט - שנקרא אח לאברהם, כדכתיב: ״אל נא תהי מריבה וגו' כי אנשים אחים אנחנו״ (בראשית י״ג:ח׳):
Rashi on Nazir 23a:20:1.english: “A brother offended” — this is Lot - For he was called a brother to Abraham, as it is written: “Let there be no strife, please... for we are brothers” (Genesis 13:8).

Rashi on Nazir 23a:2:1.english: She incurs the forty [lashes] - [The Gemara] explains this above (Nazir 21b).

Rashi on Nazir 23a:2:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר תספוג מכת מרדות - אם לא נתחייבה במלקות מן התורה, תהא לוקה מכות מדרבנן, כדי להוכיחה שלא תהא מזידה:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:2:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: She should incur lashes for rebelliousness - If she is not liable for lashes by Torah law, she shall receive rabbinic lashes, in order to rebuke her so that she does not act willfully.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:3:1.hebrew: ת"ר אישה הפרם וה' יסלח לה - במה הכתוב מדבר? אם באשה שנדרה והפר לה בעלה — סליחה זו למה? אלא כו', ע"כ באשה שהפר לה בעלה והיא לא ידעה הכתוב מדבר, דהא כבר כתיב: "ואם ביום שמוע אישה יניא אותה", דהיינו שהפר לה בידיעתה:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:3:1.english: The Sages taught: “Her husband has nullified them, and the Lord will forgive her” - Of what is the verse speaking? If [it refers] to a woman who vowed and her husband nullified [the vow] for her, why is this forgiveness [necessary]? Rather, etc. — perforce, the verse is speaking of a woman whose husband nullified [the vow] for her and she did not know, for it is already written: “And if on the day her husband hears he restrains her” (Numbers 30:9), which refers to [a case where] he nullified [it] for her with her knowledge.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:4:1.hebrew: מי שנתכוין לאכול בשר חזיר ואכל בשר טלה - גרסי':
Rashi on Nazir 23a:4:1.english: One who intended to eat pork and ate lamb - This is our reading:

Rashi on Nazir 23a:4:2.english: One who intends to eat pork - [This] is our reading.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:9:1.hebrew: דמעיקרא לאיסורא איכוון - דהא לא ידעה דהפר לה בעלה, ומשום הכי צריכה כפרה וסליחה:
Rashi on Nazir 23a:9:1.english: Because at the outset she intended [to do that which was] forbidden - For she did not know that her husband had nullified [her vow] for her, and for this reason she requires atonement and forgiveness.

Rashi on Nazir 23a:9:2.english: Where a prohibition was not established - For he thought that it was [permitted] fat.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:13:1.hebrew: פסח מיהא קעביד - משמע דאכילה גסה שמה אכילה. וקשה, דבפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פ:) קאמרי': האוכל אכילה גסה ביה"כ פטור, דלא שמה אכילה! ואומר ר"ת, דתרי ענייני אכילות גסות יש: וההוא [דיומא] — כגון שנפשו קצה באכילה מרוב שובעו; והכא — שאין נפשו קצה, אלא שאינו רעב לאכול לתיאבון:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:13:1.english: "He has at least performed [the mitzvah of] the Paschal offering" - This implies that excessive eating is considered eating. And this is difficult, for in the last chapter of Yoma (80b) we say: One who engages in excessive eating on Yom Kippur is exempt, because it is not considered eating! And Rabbeinu Tam says that there are two types of excessive eating: that one [in Yoma] is where one's soul is revolted by eating due to being overly full; whereas here, his soul is not revolted, but rather he is simply not hungry [enough] to eat with an appetite.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:14:1.hebrew: מי דמי אנן חד דרך קאמרינן - שהצדיק הולך בו, והרשע נכשל באותו דרך עצמו; [והכא] הם שני דרכים, שזה בא על אשתו וזה בא על אחותו:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:14:1.english: “Is it comparable? We said one path” - [Meaning] that the righteous walks in it and the wicked stumbles on that very same path; whereas [here] they are two paths, for this one has relations with his wife and that one has relations with his sister.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:14:2.hebrew: ללוט ושתי בנותיו הוא שנתכוון לעבירה ופושעים יכשלו בם - והיינו כמ"ד בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נח:): עובד כוכבים אסור בבתו; ואפילו למ"ד מותר — כבר פירשו [האומות] מעצמן מעריות:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:14:2.english: "To Lot and his two daughters; he who intended for the sake of a transgression, 'and transgressors stumble over them'" - And this is in accordance with the one who holds in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 58b) that a gentile is forbidden to his daughter; and even according to the one who holds [that he is] permitted, [the nations] had already separated themselves of their own accord from forbidden relations.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:15:1.hebrew: ודלמא איהו נמי לשם שמים מכוון - שלא מצינו בו שהיה שטוף בזימה. ומשני: אדרבה, שטוף היה, שנאמר: "וישא לוט", וכל הפסוק דרשינן לעבירה:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:15:1.english: "And perhaps he too intended for the sake of Heaven" - For we have not found regarding him that he was steeped in licentiousness. And [the Gemara] answers: On the contrary, he was steeped [in it], as it is stated: "And Lot lifted up [his eyes]" (Genesis 13:10), and the entire verse we expound [as referring] to transgression.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:18:1.hebrew: והא מינס קאניס - שהרי השקוהו יין, ובהאי עובדא לא היה כוונתו לעבירה כלל, ואמאי קרית ליה פושע:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:18:1.english: "But he was forced" - For they gave him wine to drink, and in this incident his intention was not for a transgression at all; why, then, do you call him a transgressor?

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:18:2.hebrew: למה נקוד על וי"ו דובקומה - לומר לך דהרי הוא כמאן דליתיה, דבקומה ידע:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:18:2.english: Why is there a dot over the vav of "uvekumah" - To tell you that [the letter vav] is as if it is not there, [so] that when she arose he knew.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:20:1.hebrew: אח נפשע מקרית עוז זה לוט - שנקרא אח לאברהם, כדכתיב: "כי אנשים אחים אנחנו". "מקרית עוז" — זה אברהם, כדכתיב: "הביטו אל צור חוצבתם":
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:20:1.english: "A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city; this is Lot" - For he is called a brother to Abraham, as it is written: "For we are men who are brothers" (Genesis 13:8). "Than a strong city" — this is Abraham, as it is written: "Look to the rock from which you were hewn" (Isaiah 51:1) [where Abraham is likened to a rock].

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:2:1.hebrew: הרי זו סופגת את הארבעים - בגמ' (דף כא:) מסיק שלא היפר לה בעלה. ופשיטא הוא! ומשום דקא בעי למיתני סיפא: "ואינה סופגת" וכו', דהוי חידושא — אע"ג דנתכוונה לאיסורא, כיון דעלה בידה היתר אינה סופגת — תנא נמי רישא: "וסופגת":
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:2:1.english: "She incurs the forty [lashes]" - In the Gemara (21b), it concludes that her husband had not nullified [the vow] for her. And [yet] it is obvious [that she is liable]! But because [the tanna] wanted to teach the latter clause: "And she does not incur [the forty lashes]," etc., which is a novel ruling — that even though she intended [to commit] a forbidden act, since what turned out in practice was permitted, she does not incur [lashes] — he also taught the first clause: "And she incurs [the forty lashes]."

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:2:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר אם אינה סופגת את הארבעים תספוג מכת מרדות - מדרבנן, שנתכוונה לאיסורא במזיד. ובפ' בתרא דמכות (דף כב.): מכות ארבעים מן התורה, אבל מכת מרדות בלי מנין, אלא מכין עד שתצא נפשו או עד שמקבל עליו. ומספקא לרבי: דהכא דלוקה על שעברה, דשמא דוקא מ' ותו לא? דדוקא כשאין רוצה לקיים אותה המצוה מכין אותו בלי מספר, אבל הכא שכבר עברה, למה תלקה יותר מדאורייתא אם לא הפר? הג"ה: גמ' — "יתיב ר"ש בן לקיש קמיה דר' יהודה נשיאה, ויתיב וקאמר: והוא שהתפיסו כולם בתוך כדי דיבור", כדמפרש והולך: כדי שאילת שלום תלמיד לרב, דהיינו "שלום עליך רבי", ג' תיבות. ה"נ יכולין שלשה אנשים להתפיס עצמן בראשון שנדר בנזיר, שכל אחד אמר "ואני", הם שלש תיבות, דאפילו האחרון תוך כדי דיבור מן הראשון. אבל הרביעי אינו יכול להתפיס עצמו בראשון, אפילו אמר "ואני", שכבר שהו כדי דיבור מן הראשון, ולכך לא חייל נזירות ארביעי:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:2:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If she does not incur the forty [lashes], she should incur lashes for rebelliousness - [This is] by rabbinic law, because she intentionally intended [to commit] a forbidden act. And in the final chapter of Makkot (22a): The forty lashes are from the Torah, but lashes for rebelliousness [makat mardut] are without count; rather, they strike [him] until his soul departs or until he accepts [compliance] upon himself. And the Rabbi is in doubt: Here, where she is lashed for [a transgression] that she already committed, perhaps [she receives] specifically forty [stripes] and no more? For specifically when someone does not wish to fulfill that [positive] commandment do they strike him without limit, but here, where she has already transgressed, why should she be lashed more than [she would be punished] by Torah law if [her husband] had not nullified [her vow]? Gloss: [The] Gemara [states on 20b]: "R. Shimon ben Lakish sat before Rabbi Yehuda Nesia, and he sat and said: And this is [only] where they all connected [their vows to the first] within the time needed for speaking [tokh kedei dibbur]" — as [the Gemara] continues to explain: [The time needed for speaking is] the time [needed for] a student's greeting of peace to a master, which is "Peace be upon you, my master [shalom aleikha, rebbi]," [consisting of] three words. Here too, three people can connect themselves to the first one who took a nazirite vow, where each one said "And I" [ve'ani], [which together] are three words, so that even the last [person] is within the time needed for speaking from the first. But the fourth [person] cannot connect himself to the first, even if he said "And I," for they have already delayed [longer than] the time needed for speaking from the first, and therefore naziriteship does not take effect upon the fourth.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:3:1.hebrew: באשה שהפר לה בעלה והיא לא ידעה הכתוב מדבר - דאי ידעה, אמאי צריכה סליחה וכפרה לכפר:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:3:1.english: “The verse is speaking of a woman whose husband nullified [her vow] and she did not know” - For if she knew [that he had nullified it], why would she need forgiveness and atonement to atone [for her]?

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:5:1.hebrew: והוא לא ידע ואשם ונשא עונו - בקרא דאשם תלוי כתיב: "ועלה בידו בשר חזיר, כגון חתיכה אחת ספק היא של חלב וספק היא של שומן" — דס"ל לת"ק, דאשם תלוי אפילו אחתיכה אחת מיחייב:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:5:1.english: “And he did not know, yet he is guilty, and shall bear his iniquity” - Regarding the verse of an uncertain guilt-offering, it is written [in the baraita]: “And pork came up in his hand, for example, one piece [of which] it is uncertain whether it is [forbidden] fat and uncertain whether it is [permitted] fat” — because the First Tanna holds that for an uncertain guilt-offering, one is liable even for a single piece.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:7:1.hebrew: איסי בן יהודה אומר [ולא ידע ואשם ונשא עונו] - ולא פי' קרא כדלעיל, אלא כגון ב' חתיכות, אחת של חלב ואחת של שומן — דס"ל לאיסי בן יהודה דלא מיחייב אשם תלוי אלא אחתיכה אחת משתי חתיכות:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:7:1.english: “Isi ben Yehuda says: [‘Though he does not know it yet he is guilty, and shall bear his iniquity’]” - And he does not explain the verse as [was explained] above, but rather [as referring to a case] such as two pieces, one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat; for Isi ben Yehuda holds that one is liable [to bring] a suspensive guilt-offering only for [a case of] one piece out of two pieces.

Tosafot on Nazir 23a:8:1.hebrew: על דבר זה יד"וו - ראשי התיבות: "ידע", "ואשם", "ונשא". הכתוב מדבר באשם תלוי:
Tosafot on Nazir 23a:8:1.english: “With regard to this matter, they should suffer” [yidvu] - [This is an] acronym of yada [“he knew”], ve’ashem [“and was guilty”], and venasa [“and bore” (Leviticus 5:17)]. The verse is speaking of a provisional guilt-offering [asham talui].
